feeds.title: Irish Economic Association News
feeds.description: The Irish Economic Association (IEA) is a national scientific body for economists in Ireland. The objective of the Association is to contribute to the development and application of economics in Ireland. It is a Company Limited by Guarantee. Anne Nolan (ESRI) is the current President of IEA.

feeds.title: RedC Research & Marketing
feeds.description: To stay updated on the Irish news, politics, finance, and more, follow RED C! RED C is Ireland's premier provider of research-based consultancy services. Founded in 2003, they provide high-quality research-based consultancy services to both blue chip and up-and-coming businesses across Ireland, the UK, and Worldwide. It is a fresh, dynamic organization whose work is rooted in sound statistical science, behavioral observation, and listening to the consumer. Their mission is to help you see clearly.

feeds.title: Finfacts Ireland Blog
feeds.description: The Finfacts economics site was launched in 1997 by Michael Hennigan. It issues news on the Irish economy, rising inequality, poverty, crime cartel, government, tech, export imports, and more.

feeds.title: TASC - Think-Tank for Action on Social Change Blog
feeds.description: The Progressive Economy is a respected and well-established forum for progressive economists and others commenting on the Irish economy. Most contributors are members of the TASC Economists' Network. TASC translates research into practice to sustain democracy and reduce inequality. It is an independent think-tank whose mission is to address inequality and sustain democracy by translating analysis into action. Their blog covers articles on different topics like fiscal policy, health, economics, inequality, banking and finance, environment, labor practice, politics, and more!

feeds.title: The Irish Economy
feeds.description: The Irish Economy delivers commentary, information, and intelligent discourse about the Irish economy. The opinions expressed on the site are personal to the individual contributors. The website personally does not endorse any of the opinions expressed on the site, nor do the employers of the contributors. The site is run on behalf of the Irish Economic Association, whose current President is Prof. Anne Nolan of the ESRI.

feeds.title: Economic Incentives
feeds.description: The Economic Incentives blog will keep you updated on all the Irish news. Economic Incentives provide shining a small light on economic reality. It aims to provide the latest Irish news on bank assets, trade, government, tax, social welfare, debt, and many more.

feeds.title: Rory O'Farrell
feeds.description: Rory O'Farrell is an economics blog that explains to the people why the costs are higher in Ireland. How the price of goods in Ireland is largely in line with other European countries, with the exception of alcohol and tobacco. It tells the people that the price of consumer goods and services is higher in Ireland due to high rents and expensive services.

feeds.title: Karl Whelan Blog
feeds.description: Karl Whelan is a Professor of Economics at University College Dublin. Before joining UCD, he worked as an economist at the Central Bank of Ireland and before that the Federal Reserve Board. In his blog, he covers categories like banking, Brexit, central banks, economic growth, education, euro crisis, European economy, fiscal compact treaty, fiscal policy, Irish economy, politics, teaching, UK economy, uncategorized, and US economy.

feeds.title: Dan McLaughlin
feeds.description: Dan McLaughlin's Blog delivers information on the Irish economy's domestic demand, Irish GDP, Irish unemployment, and more! The opinions expressed are personal to the individual contributors. Find the latest news on economic commentary and analysis. The broad categories that they cover are budget, comment of ECB, comment on Euro Era, debt, fiscal deficit, global economy, inflation, interest rates, Irish budget, Irish economy, and more.

feeds.title: Ulster Economix
feeds.description: The official blog of Ulster Economix offers views, insight, comments, and updates on the Northern Ireland economy and wider economic issues by Richard Ramsey. He is Chief Economist, Northern Ireland, at Ulster Bank and a member of the Department of Finance's Statistics Advisory Committee.

feeds.title: Notes On The Front
feeds.description: Read Notes On The Front keeps updated about the Irish, trade news, poverty and social exclusion, international, economy and business, resources, older posts, and more! It is a commentary on Irish Political Economy by Michael Taft, a researcher for SIPTU. It works to keep you updated on the latest Irish political news, analysis, and comments brought by Micheal Shaft.
